courses.title: PAUSE. VERIFY. PROTECT.
courses.summary: Learn to spot the pressure behind a suspicious message.

modules.title: WARM-UP
modules.intro: Three questions. One useful first step.

questions.prompt: A message uses a company's real logo. Does that prove it is genuine?
options: Yes. Only the company can use its logo.
No. A logo can be copied.
Yes, if the message sounds professional.
questions.explanation: Logos and writing styles are easy to copy. Verify the request through a channel you already trust.

questions.prompt: You receive an unexpected security alert. Where should you check it?
options: In the link provided by the message.
In the official app or website you open independently.
questions.explanation: Open the official service yourself. Do not let an unexpected message choose your destination.

questions.prompt: A caller asks for your one-time sign-in code. What should you do?
options: Keep the code private and verify through the service's official support.
Share it if they know your name.
Share it if they say it is urgent.
questions.explanation: A one-time code can let someone into your account. Keep it private, end the call, and verify independently.

sections.title: Pause
sections.body: Slow down when a message creates urgency, fear, or an unexpected reward. A deadline does not make a request trustworthy.

sections.title: Verify
sections.body: Open the official app, type a known website address, or call a number you already trust. Check the request through that independent channel.

sections.title: Protect
sections.body: Keep passwords and one-time sign-in codes private. Report suspicious messages using the service’s or your organization’s reporting process.
